בשם ה' נתחיל לכתוב פירוש על מסכת ברכות. 
אמר רב יהודה אמר רב מאי דכתיב כי תשא את ראש בני ישראל לפקדיהם ונתנו איש כופר נפשו לה' בפקוד אתם ולא יהיה בהם נגף בפקוד אתם. 
תניא ר' יהודה אומר שלש מצות נצטוו ישראל בכניסתן לארץ. 
להעמיד להם מלך ולהכרית זרעו של עמלק ולבנות להם בית הבחירה. 
רבי נהוראי אומר לא נאמרה פרשה זו אלא כנגד עתידין שיהיו עומדין בהן. 
וכן הוא אומר כי תשא את ראש בני ישראל לפקדיהם. 
מאי משמע דהאי פקודא לישנא דחשיבותא הוא. 
כתיב הכא בפקוד אתם וכתיב התם בפקוד אתם. 
מה להלן חשיבות אף כאן חשיבות. 
אמר רב אשי שמע מינה האי מאן דבעי למימני ישראל לא לימנינהו בגולגולתא. 
דכתיב לא יהיה בהם נגף בפקוד אתם. 
אמר רב יצחק כל המונה את ישראל עובר בלא תעשה. 
שנאמר ומספר בני ישראל יהיה כחול הים אשר לא ימד ולא יספר. 
אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק איכא דאמרי לא ימד ולא יספר. 
תניא ר' יצחק אומר מאי דכתיב ויתן את הכסף כופר נפשו. 
מלמד שכל אחד ואחד נותן מחצית השקל. 
מאי טעמא אמר רב אסי כדי שיכפרו על מעשה העגל. 
דכתיב ויתן את הכסף כופר נפשו לה' בפקוד אתם. 
אמר רב יהודה אמר רב מאי דכתיב ואתם תהיו לי ממלכת כהנים וגוי קדוש. 
אלו הדברים אשר תדבר אל בני ישראל. 
אמר רב חנינא בר פפא מאי דכתיב ויקח משה את האהל ונטה לו מחוץ למחנה. 
מלמד שהיה משה רבינו עליו השלום מפריש עצמו מן הציבור. 
כדי שיהא פנוי לעסוק בתורה ובחכמה. 
אמר רב יהודה אמר רב כל העוסק בתורה לשמה תורה נעשית לו סם חיים. 
שנאמר עץ חיים היא למחזיקים בה. 
וכל העוסק בתורה שלא לשמה תורה נעשית לו סם המות. 
שנאמר יערף כמטר לקחי. 
אמר רב רחמנא ליצלן מן האי דעתא. 
אמר רב יהודה אמר רב מאי דכתיב וידבר ה' אל משה פנים אל פנים. 
כאשר ידבר איש אל רעהו. 
מלמד שהיה הקדוש ברוך הוא מדבר עם משה בנחת. 
כדרך שאדם מדבר עם חבירו. 
אמר רב חסדא מאי דכתיב ושב אל המחנה ומשרתו יהושע בן נון נער לא ימיש מתוך האהל. 
מלמד שהיה יהושע משמש את משה בכל צרכיו. 
ולא היה זז מבית המדרש. 
אמר רב יהודה אמר רב אשרי מי שזוכה לשמש את החכמים. 
שעל ידי כך הוא זוכה ללמוד תורה ויראת שמים. 
ברוך הנותן ליעף כח ולאין אונים עצמה ירבה.

In the name of the Lord, we begin to write a commentary on Tractate Berakhot.

Rabbi Judah said in the name of Rav: What is the meaning of that which is written, "When you take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number, then they shall give every man a ransom for his soul to the Lord, when you number them; that there be no plague among them, when you number them" <note>Exodus 30:12</note>. 
It is taught: Rabbi Judah says, three commandments were the Israelites commanded upon their entry into the land: to appoint a king for themselves, to cut off the seed of Amalek, and to build for themselves the Chosen House <note>The Holy Temple</note>.
Rabbi Nehorai says: This passage was only said regarding the future, that they would stand in them <note>i.e., fulfill them later</note>.
And so it says, "When you take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number."
How is it understood that this "numbering" <term>pekudah</term> <gloss>numbering/command</gloss> is a term of importance? 
It is written here "when you number them" <term>bifkod etam</term>, and it is written there "when you number them."
Just as there it is an importance, so too here it is an importance.
Rav Ashi said: Learn from this that one who wishes to count the Israelites should not count them by the head <note>i.e., by individual tally, which is demeaning</note>.
For it is written, "that there be no plague among them when you number them."
Rav Isaac said: Anyone who counts Israel transgresses a negative commandment, as it is stated, "Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor counted" <note>Hosea 2:1</note>.
Rav Nachman bar Isaac said: There are those who say "neither measured nor counted."
It is taught: Rabbi Isaac says, what is the meaning of that which is written, "And he shall give the silver as a ransom for his soul"?
This teaches that each and every one gives half a shekel.
What is the reason? Rav Assi said: In order that they might atone for the deed of the Calf, as it is written, "And he shall give the silver as a ransom for his soul to the Lord when you number them."
Rav Judah said in the name of Rav: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation"? 
"These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel."
Rav Hanina bar Papa said: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And Moses took the tent and pitched it outside the camp"?
This teaches that Moses, our teacher—peace be upon him—would separate himself from the public so that he would be free to engage in Torah and wisdom.
Rav Judah said in the name of Rav: Whoever engages in Torah for its own sake, the Torah becomes for him a potion of life, as it is stated, "It is a tree of life to those who take hold of it."
And whoever engages in Torah not for its own sake, the Torah becomes for him a potion of death, as it is stated, "My doctrine shall drop as the rain."
Rav said: May the Merciful One save us from such a concept.
Rav Judah said in the name of Rav: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And the Lord spoke unto Moses face to face, as a man speaks unto his friend"?
This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke with Moses gently, in the way that a person speaks with his friend.
Rav Chisda said: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And he would return to the camp, but his servant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the tent"?
This teaches that Joshua would serve Moses in all his needs and would not move from the House of Study.
Rav Judah said in the name of Rav: Happy is he who merits to serve the Sages, for through this he merits to learn Torah and fear of Heaven.
Blessed be He who gives strength to the weary and increases power to the powerless.

They are called <term>vimānāni</term> <gloss>mansions</gloss> because they are characterized by distinct dimensions such as one <term>yojana</term> <gloss>a measure of distance, roughly 7-9 miles</gloss> or two <term>yojanas</term>, they shine with various jewels, have diverse colors and shapes, and through the attainment of superior splendor, they are specifically the abode of dignity. The word <term>vatthu</term> <gloss>cause or origin</gloss> means the reason for these; thus, <term>Vimānavatthu</term> <gloss>Stories of the Mansions</gloss>. The teaching that proceeds by way of such phrases as "Your seat is golden," is merely an illustration.

It should be understood as <term>Vimānavatthu</term> because this teaching occurs in dependence upon the properties of those deities—such as their appearance, enjoyments, and attendants—and the <term>kamma</term> <gloss>intentional action/deed</gloss> that generated them; or, because it is the cause of understanding the fruit of other actions. It is said, by whom was this spoken, where was it spoken, when was it spoken, and why was it spoken?

For this <term>Vimānavatthu</term> proceeds in two ways: by way of questions and by way of answers. In this, the answer-stanzas were spoken by the respective deities, but the question-stanzas were spoken partly by the Blessed One, partly by <term>Sakka</term> <gloss>the King of the gods</gloss> and others, and partly by the elder disciples. Among these, they were mostly spoken by the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, who is established in the position of the second chief disciple, who was placed by the Blessed One as the foremost among those possessing psychic power, who reached the summit of all the knowledge of the disciples' perfection—accompanied by the special qualities of the six higher knowledges and the four analytical knowledges—having accumulated the constituents of merit and knowledge for an <term>asaṃkheyya</term> <gloss>incalculable eon</gloss> and one hundred thousand <term>kappas</term> <gloss>aeons</gloss> for the status of the Blessed One's chief disciple, and having gradually fulfilled the perfections of a disciple. While speaking, he first spoke them while wandering in the realm of the gods for the benefit of the world by way of the deities' questions; then, after returning from there to the human world, he combined the questions and answers for the sake of making the fruit of merit manifest to humans.

XXXIV. Postremò Duratio alia est creata, alia increata. Increata est propria solius DEI, diciturque Æternitas; et definitur à Boëtio: *Intermi- nabilis vitæ tota simul et perfecta possessio.* Duratio creata alia est temporaria, a- lia perpetua. Temporaria est, quæ et principium habet et finem. Perpetua, quæ saltem finem non habet. Velut duratio Angelorum et Animæ rationalis, quæ et Aevum dicitur, et communiter definitur, *Permanentia rei in esse aliquando ac- cepto interminata.*

### DE QVANTITATE.

XXXV. Quantum describit Aristoteles hîc lib. 5. tex 18. *Quod est divisibile in ea, quæ insunt, quorum utrumque vel unumquodque unum quid, et hoc aliquid aptum est esse.* Id est (ut quidem P. Suarez interpretatur) quorum v- trumque aptum est naturâ suâ per sese, ut unum quoddam totum, ab alijs separatum, manere, et quidem quantum est ex vi quantitatis, eodem modo di- visibile, divisibilitate scilicet Physicâ, et naturali, vi cuius unum Corpus naturaliter expellit aliud, vel partes eius à loco, quem ante occupabant.

XXXVI. Est sententia, ut ait P. Suarez, inter Thomistas satis vul- garis, primarium quantitatis effectum formalem esse distinctionem par- tium integralium; ita ut sine quantitate nec Materia prima, nec ulla alia entitas materialis aliquas partes integrantes habeat. Thomistas ex Nostris secutus est P. Vasquez tom. 3. in 3. p. d. 190. à n. 20. Sed contrà 1. Nam sicuti vnaquæque res per se ipsam est ens, ita per se ipsam est vna, et conse- quenter divisa et distincta à quovis alio. 2. Quia aliàs procedendum foret in infinitum. Nam si vna res est distincta ab aliâ per aliam entitatem tertiam, ergo ab illâ tertiâ debebit iterum distingui per aliam quartam, et sic in infini- tum. 3. Quia Materia supponitur ad quantitatem cum totâ suâ entitate. Ergo non potest accipere partes ab illâ: cùm enim totum nihil aliud sit, quàm omnes partes, quod supponitur cum totâ entitate, debet etiam supponi cum partibus. Non potest ergo primarius effectus formalis quantitatis consistere in distinctio- ne partium.

XXXIII. Regarding Imaginary Time we judge the same as we do regarding Imaginary space, namely that it is in reality nothing, beyond the intrinsic durations of things which found various relations of distance and nearness.

XXXIV. Finally, duration is either created or uncreated. The uncreated is proper to GOD alone, and is called Eternity; and it is defined by <term>Boethius</term> <gloss>Anicius Manlius Severinus Boethius, Roman philosopher</gloss>: *The whole, simultaneous, and perfect possession of interminable life.* Created duration is either temporary or perpetual. It is temporary if it has both a beginning and an end. It is perpetual if it at least has no end. Such is the duration of Angels and the rational soul, which is also called <term>Aevum</term> <gloss>the Age or Eon</gloss>, and is commonly defined as: *The uninterrupted permanence of a thing in being once received.*

### ON QUANTITY.

XXXV. <term>Aristotle</term> describes a quantity here in Book 5, text 18: *That which is divisible into those things which are present, of which each one or every one is a certain "one," and this "something" is apt to be.* That is (as Father <term>Suarez</term> indeed interprets) of which each one is apt by its own nature in and of itself, as a certain whole, separated from others, to remain, and indeed, insofar as it is from the force of quantity, divisible in the same way, namely by physical and natural divisibility, by the force of which one Body naturally expels another, or its parts from the place which they previously occupied.

XXXVI. It is an opinion, as Father <term>Suarez</term> says, sufficiently common among the <term>Thomists</term> <gloss>followers of Thomas Aquinas</gloss>, that the primary formal effect of quantity is the distinction of integral parts; so that without quantity neither primary matter nor any other material entity has any integral parts. Father <term>Vasquez</term> <gloss>Gabriel Vázquez, Jesuit theologian</gloss> followed the Thomists among our own in Volume 3, part 3, disputation 190, from number 20. But to the contrary: 1. For just as each thing is a being in and of itself, so it is "one" in and of itself, and consequently divided and distinct from anything else. 2. Because otherwise one would have to proceed to infinity. For if one thing is distinct from another by another third entity, then it must be distinguished from that third by another fourth, and so on to infinity. 3. Because matter is presupposed for quantity with its whole entity. Therefore, it cannot receive parts from it; for since the whole is nothing other than all its parts, that which is presupposed with its whole entity must also be presupposed with its parts. Therefore, the primary formal effect of quantity cannot consist in the distinction of parts.
